source_title: Entertainment IIFA Awards 2026 Winners: 'Dhurandhar', 'Chhaava' Lead The List, Check Full Winners
source_excerpt: The 26th edition of the International Indian Film Academy (IIFA) Awards has announced its winners, celebrating achievements across Indian cinema and digital entertainment. From popular performances and technical excellence to promising debutants, the awards recognised talent across several categories. 'Dhurandhar' emerged as one of the biggest winners in the popular and technical categories, securing honours for its direction, performances, storytelling and music. 'Chhaava' also had a strong showing in the technical categories, while 'Homebound' received recognition for its adapted story. The awards also celebrated new talent, with Rasha Thadani winning Best Female Debut for 'Azaad' and Ahaan Panday taking home Best Male Debut for 'Saiyaara'. IIFA Awards 2026: Popular Category Winners 'Dhurandhar' stood out in the popular categories, receiving recognition across multiple aspects of filmmaking, including direction, acting, original storytelling and music. 'Homebound' also secured three credited wins in the Best Story (Adapted) category. Meanwhile, 'Avatar: Fire & Ash' was recognised as Best International Film, with three credited recipients associated with the award. Rahman Chhaava Special Effects (Visual) Assemblage Entertainment, Redefine Chhaava Choreography Bosco Leslie Martis (Song: Aavan Jaavan) War 2 IIFA Awards 2026: Best Debut Winners The 2026 edition also recognised emerging performers in Indian cinema. Rasha Thadani won Best Female Debut for her performance in 'Azaad', while Ahaan Panday received Best Male Debut for 'Saiyaara'. Both actors were recognised for their entry into the film industry and their performances in their respective films. Award Category Winner Film Best Female Debut Rasha Thadani Azaad Best Male Debut Ahaan Panday Saiyaara IIFA Digital Awards 2026: Film Category Winners The IIFA Digital Awards 2026 celebrated achievements in films released on digital platforms. 'Baramulla' emerged as a major winner in the film category, taking home awards for Best Picture and Best Story (Original). 'Stolen' received recognition for direction and Abhishek Banerjee's leading performance. Sanya Malhotra won for her leading performance in 'Mrs'. In the supporting performance categories, Monika Panwar was recognised for 'Nishaanchi 2', while Avinash Tiwary won for 'The Mehta Boys'.
